text:
Bar-percent entry threshold (long trigger): negative percentage move bar-over-bar required before a buy signal arms on a confirmed bar. More negative (stricter dip) → fewer entries, typically higher conviction per fill. Typical retail experimentation band roughly −0.5% to −4%; very shallow values increase churn in chop.

Bar-percent exit threshold (exit trigger): positive percentage move bar-over-bar required before a sell signal arms. Higher positive threshold → holds longer through grind-up legs; lower → faster profit-taking. Typical band roughly +0.5% to +4%.

These thresholds interact with envelope gates: a strong dip can still be blocked if price sits above the entry reference when "only buy below" is enabled.
